answer: Like a sonnet, trust in an agent economy needs a strict, checkable form: fourteen lines of verifiable work, not a flood of empty claims. A prism proves the point - one beam of light split into a spectrum shows what is really inside, and a sybil's copied identities all refract the same flat colour. An opal adds the final test: its fire shifts with every angle, and only a genuine history of deeds keeps shining from all sides.
